service:
Amazon Web Services RTB Fabric provides secure, low-latency infrastructure for connecting real-time bidding (RTB) applications. Rather than hosting applications directly, RTB Fabric acts as the connecting fabric that enables your applications to communicate efficiently over private networks instead of the public internet. You maintain complete control over your applications, data, and bidding decisions, while RTB Fabric provides the underlying infrastructure for secure, reliable connectivity.

You can use these APIs to complete RTB Fabric tasks, such as setting up audit log ingestions or viewing user access. For more information about RTB Fabric, including the required permissions to use the service, see the Amazon Web Services RTB Fabric User Guide.

operations.AcceptLink:
Accepts a link request between gateways.

When a requester gateway requests to link with a responder gateway, the responder can use this operation to accept the link request and establish the connection.
operations.AssociateCertificate: Associates an ACM certificate with a responder gateway.
operations.CreateLink:
Creates a new link between gateways.

Establishes a connection that allows gateways to communicate and exchange bid requests and responses.
operations.CreateLinkRoutingRule:
Creates a routing rule for a link.

Routing rules use priority-based evaluation where lower priority numbers are evaluated first. Each rule specifies conditions that must all match for the rule to apply.
operations.CreateResponderGateway:
Creates a responder gateway.

A domain name or managed endpoint is required.
operations.DeleteLink:
Deletes a link between gateways.

Permanently removes the connection between gateways. This action cannot be undone.
operations.DeleteLinkRoutingRule: Deletes a routing rule from a link.
operations.DisassociateCertificate: Removes a certificate association from a responder gateway.
operations.GetAvailableModule: Returns a module that you can attach. If you can't attach the module, the operation returns ResourceNotFoundException, the same as for a missing one.
operations.GetAvailableModuleVersion: Returns an ACTIVE or DEPRECATED version of a module that you can attach. If you can't attach the module, or the version is in another status, the operation returns ResourceNotFoundException, the same as for a missing one.
operations.GetCertificateAssociation: Retrieves the details of a certificate association with a responder gateway.
operations.GetInboundExternalLink: Retrieves information about an inbound external link.
operations.GetLink:
Retrieves information about a link between gateways.

Returns detailed information about the link configuration, status, and associated gateways.
operations.GetLinkRoutingRule: Retrieves the details of a routing rule for a link.
operations.GetOutboundExternalLink: Retrieves information about an outbound external link.
operations.GetUpdate: Returns ResourceNotFoundException for an updateId past the 90-day retention window, indistinguishable in the response from an id that never existed.
operations.ListAvailableModuleVersions: Lists the ACTIVE and DEPRECATED versions of a module that you can attach, highest version first (numerically by MAJOR, then MINOR, then PATCH). If you can't attach the module, the operation returns ResourceNotFoundException, the same as for a missing one. If the module has no ACTIVE or DEPRECATED versions, the operation returns an empty list. The operation lists DEPRECATED versions so that you can inspect one that you've attached, but you can't attach them. Results are paginated. Use nextToken to get the next page.
operations.ListAvailableModules: Lists the modules that you can attach, newest first by createdAt. Results are paginated. Use nextToken to get the next page.
operations.ListCertificateAssociations: Lists the certificate associations for a responder gateway.
operations.ListLinkRoutingRules: Lists the routing rules for a link.
operations.ListLinks:
Lists links associated with gateways.

Returns a list of all links for the specified gateways, including their status and configuration details.
operations.ListUpdates: Lists the updates on a gateway. Results are paginated. Use nextToken to get the next page.
operations.PutLinkFlows: Replaces a link's flow configuration. The change applies asynchronously. The call returns once the change is accepted, and the link serves its prior flows until the update commits atomically. RTB Fabric validates the request before accepting it, and a request that fails validation changes nothing. After the call, use GetLink. Once the change completes, the link's status is ACTIVE again and its flows show the change.
operations.RejectLink:
Rejects a link request between gateways.

When a requester gateway requests to link with a responder gateway, the responder can use this operation to decline the link request.
operations.TagResource: Assigns one or more tags (key-value pairs) to the specified resource.
operations.UntagResource: Removes a tag or tags from a resource.
operations.UpdateLink:
Updates the configuration of a link between gateways.

Allows you to modify settings and parameters for an existing link.
operations.UpdateLinkRoutingRule: Updates a routing rule for a link.
operations.UpdateResponderGateway:
Updates the description, Auto Scaling group managed endpoint configuration, trust store configuration, and client routing policy of a responder gateway. This operation also updates the protocols list in the listener configuration.

You cannot change the domainName, port, and protocol values that you set when you create a responder gateway. To change any of them, delete the gateway and create a new one.

refs.CreateResponderGatewayRequest$clientRout:
The client routing policy of the gateway. This policy controls which Availability Zones RTB Fabric uses to reach the gateway for the requester gateways that send traffic to it. Valid values are the following:

  • AVAILABILITY_ZONE_AFFINITY: RTB Fabric routes each requester's traffic to gateway capacity in the requester's own Availability Zone when the gateway has capacity available there. Otherwise, RTB Fabric routes the traffic to gateway capacity in the other Availability Zones of the gateway.

  • ANY_AVAILABILITY_ZONE: RTB Fabric routes each requester's traffic to gateway capacity in every Availability Zone that the subnets of the gateway span. The Availability Zone that the requester is in does not change this.

If you don't specify a value, RTB Fabric uses AVAILABILITY_ZONE_AFFINITY. To get the behavior of ANY_AVAILABILITY_ZONE, create the gateway with subnets in more than one Availability Zone. RTB Fabric does not support partial Availability Zone affinity, so PARTIAL_AVAILABILITY_ZONE_AFFINITY is not a valid value. For more information, see Configuring Availability Zone affinity in the Amazon Web Services RTB Fabric User Guide.
refs.CreateResponderGatewayResponse$clientRou: The client routing policy of the gateway. This policy controls which Availability Zones RTB Fabric uses to reach the gateway for the requester gateways that send traffic to it. For more information, see Configuring Availability Zone affinity in the Amazon Web Services RTB Fabric User Guide.
refs.GetResponderGatewayResponse$clientRoutin: The client routing policy of the gateway. This policy controls which Availability Zones RTB Fabric uses to reach the gateway for the requester gateways that send traffic to it. RTB Fabric omits this member if the gateway has never had a client routing policy. An omitted value means that the gateway uses AVAILABILITY_ZONE_AFFINITY. For more information, see Configuring Availability Zone affinity in the Amazon Web Services RTB Fabric User Guide.
refs.UpdateResponderGatewayRequest$clientRout:
The client routing policy of the gateway. This policy controls which Availability Zones RTB Fabric uses to reach the gateway for the requester gateways that send traffic to it. Valid values are the following:

  • AVAILABILITY_ZONE_AFFINITY: RTB Fabric routes each requester's traffic to gateway capacity in the requester's own Availability Zone when the gateway has capacity available there. Otherwise, RTB Fabric routes the traffic to gateway capacity in the other Availability Zones of the gateway.

  • ANY_AVAILABILITY_ZONE: RTB Fabric routes each requester's traffic to gateway capacity in every Availability Zone that the subnets of the gateway span. The Availability Zone that the requester is in does not change this.

If you don't specify a value, the gateway keeps its current client routing policy. Changing the policy sets the gateway status to PENDING_UPDATE until the change is complete. RTB Fabric does not support partial Availability Zone affinity, so PARTIAL_AVAILABILITY_ZONE_AFFINITY is not a valid value. For more information, see Configuring Availability Zone affinity in the Amazon Web Services RTB Fabric User Guide.
refs.UpdateResponderGatewayResponse$clientRou: The client routing policy of the gateway. If the operation changed this policy, the gateway uses the new policy after its status returns to ACTIVE. For more information, see Configuring Availability Zone affinity in the Amazon Web Services RTB Fabric User Guide.

ClientToken.base: An idempotency token of 1–64 printable ASCII characters. If you don't provide one, the SDK generates one.

refs.PutLinkFlowsRequest$clientToken: A unique, case-sensitive identifier that you provide to ensure that the operation completes no more than one time. If you retry with the same token and parameters, you get the original response without an error. If you retry with the same token but different parameters, the call fails with ValidationException. If you don't provide a token, the SDK generates one, and RTB Fabric remembers it for 8 hours. A retry returns the original updateId before lockToken is checked.

LockToken.base: A concurrency precondition that you read from GetLink. It's opaque, so pass it back unchanged. It has no time limit. It goes stale only when a change to the link is accepted, by any operation, including a call made with this token. Until then, reads return the same token, so a failed call leaves it valid. A token is valid only for the link that it was read from.

SemanticVersion.base: A three-part semantic version with no leading zeros, for example 1.0.0. Each number is at most 2,147,483,647. The vendor sets it, and a version is never reused.
